title: Backpropagation Through a Dense Layer
learning_objectives: Derive dX, dW and db for Y = XW + b from the chain rule
Compute the mean-squared-error loss and its gradient
Check every gradient shape against its parameter's shape
entry_point: dense_backward(X, W, dY); relu_backward(Z, dA); mse_and_grad(Y_hat, Y); two_layer_grads(X, Y, params)
hints: `relu_backward` is `dA * (Z > 0)`; the MSE gradient is `2 * diff / diff.size`.
Forward: `Z1 = X @ W1 + b1`, `H = np.maximum(Z1, 0)`, `Y_hat = H @ W2 + b2`; backward: dense (layer 2) → relu → dense (layer 1).

failure_feedback.advice: Use `dW = X.T @ dY`, `db = dY.sum(axis=0)`, `dX = dY @ W.T`.
Each gradient must have the shape of what it differentiates.
Pass the gradient only where Z > 0.
Divide by the total number of entries: `2 * diff / diff.size`.
Run the forward pass, then dense (layer 2) → ReLU → dense (layer 1).
